summary: Reverse the nodes of a linked list between positions left and right (1-indexed).
mainInsight: Walk to the node before position left, reverse exactly right - left + 1 nodes with the standard prev/curr/next loop, then reconnect the reversed segment to the part before and after it. A dummy head handles left = 1.

approaches.name: Copy to an array
approaches.summary: Reverse a slice of values and rebuild.

approaches.name: In-place reversal of a segment
approaches.summary: Reverse the sub-list pointers and relink the ends.

personalSolution.approach: In-place reversal of a segment with a dummy head
personalSolution.notes: Optimal; your comments show the array-based brute force.

promptVariants: What technique reverses a sub-list in place?
Which pointers do you need to relink afterwards?
options: 3-pointer reversal, then reconnect both ends of the sub-list
Recursion on the whole list, reversing every single node
Sorting the values of the sub-list and relinking them
A stack of all the list's nodes, popped to relink them
cards.answer: 3-pointer reversal, then reconnect both ends of the sub-list
cards.explanation: After reversing, the old left node must point to the node after the segment and the node before left must point to the new segment head.

promptVariants: After the reversal loop, what do `prev`, `curr` and `tail` point to?
Which nodes are used for the final relinking?
cards.answer: prev is the new head of the reversed segment (the old right node), curr is the first node after the segment, and tail (the old left node) is now the segment's last node. So tail.next = curr and leftNode.next = prev reconnect everything.
cards.explanation: leftNode is the node before the segment (dummy if left = 1).
At most one pass to reach left and one over the segment.

promptVariants: Why create `dummy = ListNode(0, head)` and what does the first for-loop do?
cards.code:
dummy = ListNode(0, head)
leftNode = dummy
for _ in range(left - 1):
    leftNode = leftNode.next
prev = None
curr = leftNode.next
tail = leftNode.next
for _ in range(right - left + 1):
    nextt = curr.next
    curr.next = prev
    prev = curr
    curr = nextt
tail.next = curr
leftNode.next = prev
cards.answer: The dummy gives a node before position 1, so leftNode.next = prev works uniformly even when the head itself is reversed. The first loop advances leftNode to the node just before position left.

options: It must reverse the whole list
cards.explanation: Reversing one node is a no-op; the early return handles it. (Nothing changes: a single node reversed is itself)
